label: H.R. 6484

latest_action.text: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 13 - 10.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Kids Online Safety Act establishes requirements for internet platforms that feature user-generated content, interaction, and design features promoting user engagement to protect minors (individuals under 17) and children (individuals under 13). It requires covered platforms to implement reasonable measures to prevent specific harms to minors, provide user and parental safeguards, submit to annual independent audits, and adhere to enforcement mechanisms overseen by the Federal Trade Commission and State attorneys general.

affected_groups.effect: Individuals under 17 receive default safeguards on covered platforms to limit communication, restrict compulsive design features, and receive notice of parental controls. Children under 13 have parental tools enabled by default.
Parents receive accessible tools to manage privacy and account settings for children, restrict purchases, view time-spent metrics, and limit time spent on platforms.

Websites, software, applications, or electronic services featuring searchable user-generated content and engagement-promoting design features must establish preventive measures, offer safeguards, undergo annual audits, and face enforcement actions for violations.
Empowered to enforce the Act as an unfair or deceptive practice, with State attorneys general able to bring civil actions on behalf of state residents after notifying the Commission.
affected_groups.group: Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General

key_provisions: Covered platforms must establish policies and procedures to address harms to minors including physical violence, sexual exploitation and abuse, distribution or use of narcotic drugs, tobacco, cannabis, alcohol, or gambling, and financial harm from deceptive practices.

Platforms must provide readily accessible safeguards for minors to limit communication from other users and limit design features causing compulsive usage, with the most protective settings enabled by default for known minors.
Platforms must provide parental tools allowing parents to view or change privacy settings (for children), restrict purchases, and monitor or restrict time spent on the platform.
Platforms must provide a reporting mechanism and electronic point of contact for harms to minors, with substantive responses required within 10 days or promptly for imminent threats.
Platforms are prohibited from facilitating the advertising of narcotic drugs, cannabis, tobacco products, gambling, or alcohol to known minors.
Platforms must undergo annual independent third-party audits and submit the results to the Federal Trade Commission.
The Secretary of Commerce must establish a Kids Online Safety Council to submit reports and recommendations to Congress regarding the online safety of minors.
missing_information: Specific financial penalties or fine amounts for violating the Act are not stated in the text.
The exact criteria or metrics independent auditors must use beyond general statutory guidelines are not fully detailed.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Kids Online Safety Act establishes requirements for internet platforms that feature user-generated content, interaction, and design features promoting user engagement to protect minors (individuals under 17) and children (individuals under 13). It requires covered platforms to implement reasonable measures to prevent specific harms to minors, provide user and parental safeguards, submit to annual independent audits, and adhere to enforcement mechanisms overseen by the Federal Trade Commission and State attorneys general.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates comprehensive federal standards for internet platforms regarding the safety, privacy, and engagement features used by minors. By combining mandatory platform safeguards, parental control tools, annual independent audits, and dual federal-state enforcement, it introduces major oversight into how user-generated content platforms operate for younger demographics.
